audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings say Defiant Dance is a 'W heal-block' or that she 'heals burst with her W'. Defiant Dance neither heals nor blocks healing.
audit.why: Riot's Defiant Dance text: 'Irelia charges a strike that deals more damage as she charges. She takes reduced physical damage during the charge' — 20/18/16/14/12. The heal is on Bladesurge, which 'dashes forward to strike her target, healing herself'. Getting this wrong costs you the trade twice over: Pantheon's damage is entirely physical, so dumping the burst into a charging Defiant Dance is the single worst moment to commit, and it is the moment the page implicitly recommends.
audit.corrected: Defiant Dance reduces PHYSICAL damage while she charges — never spend the burst into it; her healing is Bladesurge's.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Mark is never explained, so the Bladesurge reset chain reads as something she just gets for free.
audit.why: Riot's Flawless Duet: enemies caught between the two converging blades are 'damaged, stunned and Marked'. Riot's Bladesurge: 'If the target is Marked or dies to Bladesurge, its cooldown refreshes.' The Mark is the whole engine — deny the 16s stun and the reset chain does not start. And that same stun is what cancels an Aegis Assault channel, which _missing-interactions.json flags.
audit.corrected: Flawless Duet's stun also Marks you, and a Mark is what refreshes Bladesurge — dodge the 16s and the chain never begins.

audit.whatIsWrong: Coverage records that no Irelia ability is named in the content layer, and no cooldown appears anywhere.
audit.why: Bladesurge 10s at 600, Defiant Dance 20s at 825, Flawless Duet 16s at 850, Vanguard's Edge 125s at 950 — and the ultimate leaves a wall of blades that damages and slows anything walking through it, which the page never mentions even though it decides whether you can disengage after a failed all-in.
audit.corrected: Numbers throughout; Vanguard's Edge's blade wall named as the disengage problem.

audit.why: 49.78% over 1143 games with the chart giving Pantheon everything except level 6. Honest: he owns the levels before Flawless Duet exists, and her level 6 is the flip.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are yours. At 1 your point-and-click W stun plus Q taps is one of the strongest all-ins in the game, and she has no Q-reset dashes yet to escape it — punish any step-up to last-hit. At 2 (W+Q) you spike for a hard all-in, and at 3 with all three basics you have a premier kill window. Hold-aim your Q from max range so she eats poke trying to farm, and angle your E directional block toward her empowered autos when she Q-dashes in so the trade comes back even or better.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are yours. At 1 Shield Vault's leap-stun plus Q taps is one of the strongest all-ins in the game and Bladesurge has no Mark to reset off — punish any step-up. At 2 you spike, at 3 you have a premier kill window. Hold-aim Comet Spear from max range, and watch her W: Defiant Dance reduces PHYSICAL damage while she charges, and every point of your damage is physical, so never burst into it. Face her instead and let Aegis Assault eat the strike when it releases.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay roughly even — you still control range with held Q and E blocks, but her Q-reset chaining through the wave lets her dodge your W and trade back without committing. The real shift is 6: her ultimate stun plus a full Q-reset combo snowballs trades you used to end with a single W, and she heals burst with her W. Don't over-commit hoping for the old level-2 kill; if you can't get a clean W-stun angle, use Grand Starfall to leave the lane and cash your early lead into other lanes instead.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay roughly even — held Q keeps range, but Bladesurge resets through the wave on 10s. The chain has one key though: Flawless Duet's stun is what MARKS you, and a Mark is what refreshes Bladesurge, so dodging her 16s E stops the whole engine. It also cancels an Aegis Assault channel, so never start one into it. At 6 Vanguard's Edge Marks you at 125s and leaves a wall of blades that damages and slows anything walking through it, so a failed all-in has no exit. Roam with Grand Starfall and cash the early lead in another lane instead.

edits.before: You own level 1 outright — point-and-click W stun plus Q damage with no Q-reset for her to escape with means you win any all-in.
edits.after: You own level 1 outright — Shield Vault's leap-stun plus Q damage, with no Mark for Bladesurge to reset off, wins any all-in.

edits.before: At 6 her ultimate stun plus full Q-reset combo and W heal-block beat your single W all-in — her clearest lead window.
edits.after: At 6 Vanguard's Edge Marks you, feeds the Bladesurge chain and walls your exit — her clearest lead window in the lane.

notes: The repeated 'W heal-block' was a fabricated mechanic and an actively harmful one. Defiant Dance takes REDUCED PHYSICAL DAMAGE while charging, and Pantheon deals nothing but physical damage — so the moment the page treated as neutral is the worst possible moment to commit. Her actual healing is on Bladesurge, which is the anti-heal case in _missing-interactions.json. The second gap was the Mark: Flawless Duet stuns AND Marks, and a Mark is what refreshes Bladesurge, so the reset chain the page describes as inevitable is really downstream of one 16-second skillshot. That same stun is what cancels an Aegis Assault channel.
